passage:
Dear Seema Masi,
I'm writing because I can't say this out loud. For the past few days everything has felt pointless. I wake up already tired. I keep going over the mistake I made in the exam, and I am so angry at myself that I can hardly look in the mirror. It hasn't stopped for days. I don't think anyone would understand.
But I know you would listen. I don't want to keep this to myself any more. Could you come with me to see the school counsellor on Monday? I'm scared to go alone. And if the feelings ever get frightening and I feel unsafe, I will call the helpline number printed in my school diary right away.
Thank you for reading this.
Leela

Under it, in Masi's handwriting that evening: "Leela, I'm here now, downstairs. We'll talk tonight and I'll stay till you sleep. One exam doesn't change how loved you are. Monday, we go together."

qa.q: Who does Leela ask to come along to the school counsellor?
qa.a: Leela asks Seema Masi to come along.

qa.q: Why is Leela writing a letter instead of speaking?
qa.a: Leela feels scared and alone, sure no one would understand, so writing is easier than speaking; Leela trusts Seema Masi to listen.

qa.q: What should Leela do if the feelings become frightening?
qa.a: Leela should call the helpline number in the school diary right away and tell a trusted adult, as the letter promises.

qa.q: How does Seema Masi respond to the letter?
qa.a: Seema Masi comes that same evening, promises to stay and talk until Leela sleeps, says Leela is still loved, and will go along on Monday.

grounding: A teen who feels everything is pointless and is very angry at themself reaches out in a letter to a trusted adult and plans to see a counsellor and use a helpline if unsafe.

passage:
Thursday night. For almost two weeks everything has felt grey and pointless. I've been hating myself for everything: the maths test, the way I talk, even for being tired. Today in the library I wrote 'what's the point of me' in the back of my rough book, and Irfan saw it. He didn't laugh. He said, 'Come with me,' and walked me straight to Mrs Dsouza, the counsellor. I almost ran. But I told her. She listened, said I wasn't a burden, and said feelings like this can change with help. She called Ammi while I sat there, and Ammi came to school within the hour. Mrs Dsouza gave us a helpline number that's open all night and booked me in with a doctor tomorrow. Tonight Ammi sat on my bed till late and made me promise to wake her if it gets bad. I don't feel fixed. But I'm not carrying it alone any more.
- Rafiq

qa.q: What did Rafiq write in the back of the rough book?
How had Rafiq been feeling for almost two weeks?
qa.a: Rafiq felt hopeless and full of self-hatred, with everything seeming grey and pointless.

qa.q: Why was going to Mrs Dsouza right away the wise step?
qa.a: Feelings like these need a trusted adult now; she involved Ammi, a helpline and a doctor the same day.

qa.q: How did Irfan respond when he saw what Rafiq wrote?
qa.a: He took it seriously, didn't laugh, and walked Rafiq straight to the counsellor 🤍

grounding: A diary of a teen feeling hopeless and self-hating for days, telling a counsellor the same day and getting family, helpline and doctor support.

passage:
Ritu: are you awake
Yusuf: yeah. what's up
Ritu: I don't know. everything feels pointless. I've hated myself all week. today I just stayed in bed
Yusuf: I'm really glad you told me. are you safe right now?
Ritu: I think so. I just don't see the point of anything
Yusuf: ok. this is too big for just us two. can you wake your mum now? I'll stay on chat
Ritu: she'll be upset
Yusuf: she'd be more upset not knowing. please. or I can ask my dad to call her
Ritu: ok. going
Ten minutes later:
Ritu: she's here. she hugged me. she called the helpline number from school and I talked to someone. they were kind
Ritu: mum's sleeping in my room tonight and we're seeing the counsellor tomorrow first thing
Yusuf: I'm so proud of you. message me anytime
Ritu: thank you for not letting me keep it in

qa.q: Who did Ritu wake after chatting with Yusuf?
How was Ritu feeling when messaging Yusuf?
qa.a: Ritu felt hopeless and full of self-hatred, seeing no point in anything after a week of it.

qa.q: What did Yusuf do that was right?
qa.a: Yusuf asked if Ritu was safe, said it was too big to keep between friends, and pushed for waking Mum that night.
She hugs Ritu, calls the helpline straight away, and stays close that night before the counsellor visit.

grounding: A night chat where a teen shares hopelessness and self-hatred, and a friend gets a parent and a helpline involved the same night.
